Apple's annual September iPhone event is still about two months away, but this year will be different. In September, Apple will not unveil the entire iPhone lineup at once — only the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a brand-new foldable iPhone will be announced first.

The iPhone lineup continues to expand

Over the past few years, the iPhone product line has gradually grown. Not too long ago, only three new models were launched each year: the iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, and iPhone 11 Pro Max. By 2020, with the addition of the iPhone 12 mini, the number of models released annually increased to four. In 2022, the iPhone 12 mini was replaced by the iPhone 14 Plus, which was later succeeded by the iPhone Air.

With the arrival of the iPhone 16e, the number of models released each year further increased to five. Once the iPhone Ultra launches, the annual iPhone lineup will expand to six models. With so many models, unveiling them all at once would certainly make the stage extremely crowded.

Therefore, Apple has decided to adopt a phased launch strategy.

Two iPhone events: Fall and Spring

The iPhone 18 series will include six models: iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone Ultra.

The logic behind this phased strategy is clear: flagship models debut in the fall, while mid-range and entry-level models appear in the spring. The specific安排 is as follows:

  • Fall 2026: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Ultra
  • Spring 2027: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

Whenever the iPhone lineup expanded to four models, the additional model always had disappointing sales — whether it was the iPhone mini or the iPhone Plus. So Apple believes it makes perfect sense to clearly segment the product line and give that extra model its own moment in the spotlight.

However, when it comes to the iPhone 18, the situation will be slightly different. Reports suggest Apple is working hard to unify the production processes of the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, so the differences between the two phones may be significantly narrowed.

It remains unclear whether this approach will bring major upgrades to the iPhone 18e or result in some downgrades for the iPhone 18 — but the divide between the two phones may ultimately come down to just details like the display panel and cameras.

Summary

In summary, assuming the iPhone Air isn't eventually discontinued (which I certainly hope won't happen) — this is the new landscape for the iPhone lineup going forward. Three in the fall, three in the spring. The ultimate goal is to allow Apple to better stagger its release schedule and get products into the hands of the right consumers.

Another possible outcome is that the average selling price of iPhones will rise, because any consumer looking to capitalize on the new hardware buzz will inevitably have to buy the iPhone 18 Pro rather than a cheaper model.

Whether the phased launch strategy can truly drive sales across all models remains to be seen, but these are some initial observations.

What are your thoughts on Apple's phased iPhone launch approach? Would you buy a new iPhone in the fall or wait until spring? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
